caveats: Simulation. The instrument parameters are measured (table below); the acquisitions are simulated, and the model spectrum is illustrative. Two features sit at flight times of peaks actually observed (27.75 and 51.11 us); nothing is mass-identified.

Each Monte Carlo gain is a ratio of two standard deviations from 400 trials: relative standard error ~5 %, drawn as error bars. A time saving at equal SNR goes as the gain squared, so its error is twice that.
The excess noise F cancels in the gain (panel 1) but costs sqrt(F) in the absolute SNR of both modes (panel 2). Both are true; neither panel should be read as the other.
